newsitem.title: NIGERIA: U.S. defends itself from Nigerian visa protests.
newsitem.headline: U.S. defends itself from Nigerian visa protests.

text.p: The United States on Friday rejected complaints by Nigeria's military government about the treatment of Nigerians seeking visas, saying it uses the same procedures everywhere in the world.

"The embassy of the United States wishes to assure all Nigerians that the procedure its consular section follows when an individual applies for a U.S. visa is standard worldwide administrative practice," it said in a statement.

The foreign ministry's director-general Jibrin Chinade told representatives of the British and U.S. embassies in the capital Abuja this week the government was unhappy at the treatment of Nigerians seeking visas.
"The government is very unhappy with the way and manner in which Nigerians who apply for visas are treated by many countries," said Chinade, who also protested at the visa fees.
The U.S. embassy replied that the $20 or the local currency equivalent charged amounted to one percent of the cost of an air ticket to the United States from Nigeria.
"The embassy wishes to note that this fee is in many cases less than the charges the government of Nigeria levies on Americans applying for Nigerian visas in the United States," it said.
Military-ruled Nigeria's relations with Western nations are strained over the lack of democracy and alleged human rights abuses.
Nationals of the populous African nation also have a reputation abroad of sharp practices which has made it difficult for even genuine travellers to secure visas.
